title: Ensuring Safety
text: “Oh…”
When I looked ahead, I saw men in robes staring at us in astonishment.
“What’s going on?”
“Huh?”

How many times have I heard this line now? Starting with my Father, Ren and Itsuki are having the same conversation as always. In the meantime, let’s sort out the situation. That’s what my Father asked me to do last time.

First off, we—the Four Holy Heroes—were summoned… Melromarc didn’t like that my Father was among us, so he ostracized him. While the heroes hadn’t yet had a chance to build relationships with one another, Melromarc framed my Father for a crime he didn’t commit, trying to leave him penniless and homeless.

Initially, relying on my knowledge of the future, I saved my father from the false accusation. After that, I sent my father off when he received a recruitment offer from Siltvelt, and at the border fortress, he was struck down by Ceremonial Magic cast by Melromarc’s army and died… This is the first loop since the cycle began.

Next, after being summoned here, when I raised a fuss in the throne room after my Father was lured into a trap, that Trash—whose plan had been exposed—immediately plotted to eliminate both my Father and me. However, thanks to Éclair and me, we were able to thwart that plot before it happened, but we headed for Siltvelt to escape the pursuers as wanted fugitives. After that, just as we’d safely reached Siltvelt, Takt arrived as an assassin sent by the Crimson Swine. We fought him off, which turned Takt’s pig followers into a band of stragglers and sparked a war. Ultimately, the loop restarted when Itsuki was killed by Smoked Meat.
That covers the main events as I remember them.
So, what should I do first? What did my Father say? He asked me to act in a way that would make my knowledge of the future useful.

Let’s think this through carefully, just as Father said. If I cause a commotion in the Throne Room, Father’s life will be in danger. If I act too conspicuously, Trash and the Three Heroes Church will attack him.

Next, what would happen if I tried to go to another country? Judging by the first and second instances, they’d likely attack me there as well—it’s dangerous. So… first, I need to wait until my Father has fully matured and ensure his safety.
“Hey.”
My Father nudged me with his elbow.
“What is it?”
“Introduce yourself.”
It seems I’d already introduced myself in the Throne Room while I was silently lost in thought.
“My name is Motoyasu Kitamura—”
I could make a scene right now, but if I give the wrong impression, they might start treating me with suspicion too. So, I’d better keep quiet for now.
“Hmm… Ren, Motoyasu, and Itsuki, then?”
“Your Majesty, you’re forgetting me.”
“Oh, my apologies. Lord Naofumi.”
By doing this, the time will come when I can talk with my Father and the others in the same room. Right now, my Father is listening to the explanation of Status Magic… “Ren” and is quite surprised.
I’ll quietly search for the right moment to help my Father and a way to gain his trust. Even if I blurt out everything about the future, my Father won’t believe me. The loops so far have proven that.

When will he believe me? …On the first day of our journey, there were so many disruptions that I don’t even know where my Father was. In fact, I don’t even know which inn Father is staying at. There’s just too little information.

Based on what Father said last time, there’s a high chance we’ll end up looping again due to some unforeseen circumstance. In that case, to gather as much information as possible, I should not only find out which inn Father is staying at but also, if possible, keep track of Ren and Itsuki’s actions—at least on the first day—as that will be useful later on. Their initial actions, in particular, are bound to have a significant impact down the line.

Now, let’s get back to the matter at hand. The question is: when, specifically, will my Father come to believe me? The answer is when he’s been falsely accused and has reached the point where he can’t trust anything or anyone. It makes me feel sick to my stomach, but in order to earn my Father’s trust… that moment—when I help him—is the only time I can use my knowledge of the future.

The problem is… it’ll be a while before my Father believes what I have to say. Setting that aside for now, assuming my Father survives, what’s the best course of action? I, Motoyasu, will do my best to avoid starting any unnecessary wars.

There are several possible approaches. First is Zeltoble, the mercenary nation where Ren fled. It’s a place shrouded in darkness—the perfect place to hide. It’s also ideal for earning money by fighting in the colosseum.

However, it’s somewhat doubtful that Melromarc—and, of course, the Three Heroes Church—would just stand by and watch. We can’t completely rule out the possibility that Melromarc might declare war on Zeltoble. Zeltoble might even offer my Father up as a sacrifice to avoid war.

Besides, I have a feeling that if we stay silent, Takt will start making his move. No… based on my experience from previous loops, it’s unlikely that Takt will come after us. However, it’s also true that we should eliminate Takt sooner rather than later. That said, the timing of Takt’s elimination is crucial. He’s not only the cause of the war, but we’ll also be swamped dealing with the remnants afterward.

The downside to this plan is that the knowledge of the future contained in Father’s words won’t be of much use. Father’s words are absolute—he never says anything wrong. Given that, heading to Zeltoble isn’t an option at this point.

The next possibility is Faubrey… I suppose. There’s a risk of running into Takt, but even Melromarc wouldn’t dare commit the barbaric act of declaring war on Faubrey, a nation considered a major power. After all, back when I was still chasing after a pig’s rear end, it was the Queen of Melromarc and the Four Holy Sects from Faubrey who played key roles in the case that proved my Father’s innocence.
The problem is that our knowledge of the future isn’t much help here either. At best, we can just take out Takt as soon as possible.
……You need to think this through more carefully. No war broke out……?

Come to think of it, if the Queen of Melromarc returns to this country, the rampage of the Crimson Swine and Trash will be curbed. Consequently, Father’s safety would be guaranteed as a result. Sure, the Three Heroes Church might cause some trouble before that, but things should proceed smoothly. Based on what we know about the original world, if we eliminate Takt after the Phoenix Battle, war might not break out after all.

I see. Instead of fleeing to another country—though it’s a bit risky—adopting a wait-and-see strategy in Melromarc is one option. Didn’t my Father initially gather funds to prepare for the turmoil? He only ended up on the run because of the incident that followed; until then, he was relatively safe. At this point, this is the best course of action.

Perhaps I should secretly eliminate the troublemakers first to ensure the Father’s personal safety. In the meantime, the Father can go peddling to raise funds. By moving from place to place, we’ll make it harder for the Three Heroes Church to track him down.

However… there remains one major problem: Motoyasu’s objective. Last time, I still couldn’t find Filo-tan in the end—even after buying up every single Filolial-sama in the Monster Merchant’s tent. What could this mean?

The only possibilities are that either my Father bought them from the Monster Merchant, or someone else snapped them up before I could. But it would be quite a struggle to gather enough money to buy them all up without resorting to underhanded methods.
“I’ll go gather some companions. After all, the sun is already setting. Hero, you should rest up today and set out tomorrow. I’ll gather some promising candidates who might join us by then.”
“Thank you.”

My father and the others bowed, and we were led to a private room to rest. Just as I thought. If you make too much of a commotion in the Throne Room, you’ll be ushered into a separate room and set up for a trap. Come to think of it, what should we do about Éclair? Do we need to rescue Éclair, who’s being held in the castle dungeon?
…Rescuing her would probably draw unnecessary attention. Besides, knowing Éclair, she’d likely try to convince my Father to take her to another country for “safety’s sake.” That would lead to war.
In that case, let’s not rescue Éclair. In the first world, she was always around Big Sister for one reason or another, so I’m sure she’ll be fine.
